summary: Streaming chat halts mid-generation for long-turn responses (SSE) in eu-west
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NoteCraft reports that SSE streaming sessions frequently halt partway through long generated responses (~1200-2500 tokens). The client observes the HTTP/1.1 connection closing without a final 'data: [DONE]' frame; no 5xx is returned by the API gateway.

Impact:
- Affects NoteCraft's production integration for assistant sessions used in content drafting (enterprise tier).
- Users see partial responses and need to re-query; higher token usage and degraded UX.
- Reported ~8-12 times/day for this customer since 2026-03-10.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API, prod, region eu-west.
- Customer calls model rdm-13b-q8_0 with stream=true and chunk_size=1024 on a long-turn prompt.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open SSE to POST /v1/chat/stream with model=rdm-13b-q8_0, stream=true, max_tokens=3000.
2) Send a prompt designed for multi-paragraph generation (~3-4k input+expected output).
3) Observe streaming output for ~10-30s then abrupt close of connection from server side.
4) No final [DONE] event is received.

Observed behavior:
- Client sees 'connection closed' and SSE stops delivering tokens. No 5xx body.
- In some instances client receives a single HTTP 204 (no body) after reconnect attempt.
- Customer-side websocket client shows close code 1006 (abnormal) when using WS gateway.

Expected behavior:
- Stream continues until model finishes and server emits final data:[DONE] event, or an explicit error with 5xx/429 is returned.

Workaround used by customer:
- Shorten max_tokens to <1200 or disable streaming and poll for the full response (costly and increases latency).

Relevant logs/headers (customer attached):
- Upstream request id: req-eu-47a2a0b3
- Observed server connection close at ~t=18.4s, no application-level error.
- Proxy trace: streaming-proxy timed out read from backend after 10s of inactivity on the connection handling the chunked response.

Notes:
- Customer is on enterprise contract with 24/7 support.
- Incident spikes align with increased traffic on our eu-west serving pool starting 2026-03-10.
comments: Support - Elena Park (2026-03-12): Opened after initial triage with NoteCraft. Customer supplied cURL reproducer and raw SSE capture. Marking P1 due to enterprise SLA and frequency.

SRE - Mateo Ruiz (2026-03-12): Acknowledged. Collecting proxy and load balancer traces for the time window (req-eu-47a2a0b3). Tentatively suspect streaming-proxy read timeouts and KV-cache eviction interactions when responses exceed 1024-token chunks.

Customer - NoteCraft (2026-03-12): Provided additional traces showing close events occur at different token boundaries; reported it happens on both browser and server SDK clients. They can reproduce ~30% of attempts with their standard prompt set.

SRE - Mateo Ruiz (2026-03-12): Captured proxy logs: 'streaming-proxy: read timeout after 10s waiting for chunk', but backend serving-runtime logs show continuous generation and tokens emitted to local FIFO; mismatch suggests intermittent disconnect between serving-runtime socket and streaming-proxy forwarder.

Infra - Priya Kaur (2026-03-12): Noted there was a restart of one eu-west serving node pool on 2026-03-10 for a routine kernel patch. Rolling restart may have left some proxy connections in SYN-RCVD causing higher latencies for long-lived SSE flows.

SRE - Mateo Ruiz (2026-03-13): Reproduced locally by forcing larger KV cache sweeps during generation; observed that when cache compaction runs concurrently with long-response generation, the serving-runtime stalls writing to its stdout socket for ~9-11s which triggers proxy read timeout. Patch proposed to extend proxy read idle timeout and to add backpressure metrics.

Support - Elena Park (2026-03-13): Sent customer the temporary mitigation steps: 1) set stream_idle_timeout to 25s via per-customer routing policy, 2) advised to pin model to rdm-13b-16k as a test which shows reduced incidence. Customer will test over next 24h.

SRE - Mateo Ruiz (2026-03-13): Linked internal PR for short-term proxy timeout bump: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4123. Also opened INT-621 to track root-cause work for KV cache compaction coordinating with streaming-forwarders.
investigation_notes: 01) Reproduced failure locally with stress harness targeting long token streams and induced KV cache compaction; observed forwarder read stalls ~9-11s.
02) Proxy read timeout default is 10s; when serving-runtime stalls under compaction, proxy drops connection without logging backend error.
03) No evidence of TLS termination errors or upstream 5xx from NLB. Load balancer metrics show elevated connection churn during time window.
04) Affected nodes correlate with a canary kernel update restart on 2026-03-10; service mesh sidecars may have older backpressure handling causing queueing spikes.
05) Temporary mitigation: bump streaming-proxy read timeout to 30s for affected tenant routes; add metric export for 'generator-backpressure-seconds' to trace stalls.
next_steps: 1) Deploy proxy timeout bump to eu-west for NoteCraft route (short-term, today).
2) Merge PR adding backpressure metrics and guarded writes in serving-runtime (SRE review required).
3) Run extended soak test with KV cache compaction enabled and long-turn prompts (48h).
4) If soak stable, roll change globally and backfill release notes.
resolution: Ongoing - short-term proxy timeout increase applied to customer route; patch for guarded writes in review. Awaiting customer confirmation over 24h test window.
file_notes: Created by support agent after phone call with customer. Keep ticket lean; more detailed RCA in INT-621 and confluence link above.
